cards.text: This is a Maskil of Asaph, one of Israel's psalm writers, and he's talking straight to God. No warm-up. No "How's Your week going?" His very first line: “Why have You rejected us forever, O God?”

cards.question: Asaph asks why God's anger smolders against His people. What does Asaph call them?

cards.text: Then Asaph asks God to remember His congregation. These are the people God purchased long ago and redeemed as the tribe of His inheritance.

cards.question: Asaph reminds God of Mount ___, the place where He dwells.

cards.text: Now Asaph asks God to turn His steps to the everlasting ruins. It's like walking somebody through your place after a break-in, except this is God's own sanctuary.

cards.question: Asaph says the enemy damaged only a few things in God's sanctuary.

cards.text: Asaph tells God what happened in there. God's foes ROARED inside His meeting place, then unfurled their banners as signs, like they own the place.

cards.question: Asaph paints a picture of the foes tearing through God's meeting place. They're like men doing what?

answers.text: Wielding axes in a thicket of trees
Tearing down a tent in the wind
Breaking pots in a potter's house

cards.text: They smash all the carvings with hatchets and picks. Friend, my edges wore down slowly over years of baking, and I thought I had it rough.

cards.question: After smashing the carvings, what do the enemies do to the sanctuary itself?

cards.text: Asaph even tells God what the enemies were thinking. They said in their hearts, “We will crush them completely.”

cards.question: The enemy stopped at the sanctuary and left every other place where God met His people standing.
With the meeting places burned, Asaph says there are no signs left for God's people to see. Who else is gone?

cards.text: And none of them knows how long this will last. That's being on hold with NO voice telling you how many callers are ahead of you, just the music, on repeat.

cards.question: Asaph cries out to God, asking how long the enemy will ___ Him.
Asaph says the foe's insults are aimed at God's own name.

cards.text: Then Asaph asks why God withdraws His strong right hand. He's not asking for a pep talk. He's asking for that hand.

cards.question: What does Asaph ask God to do with His strong right hand?

answers.text: Stretch it out to destroy the enemy
Raise it up to bless the land

cards.text: Then, right in the middle of all those hard questions, the psalm turns on one little word: Yet. Three letters. Changes EVERYTHING.

cards.question: After everything he's seen, Asaph still calls God his King from ancient times.

cards.text: Asaph starts listing what this King has done. God divided the sea by His strength and smashed the heads of the dragons of the sea.

cards.question: Asaph names one more creature whose heads God crushed. Which one?

cards.text: God fed Leviathan to the creatures of the desert. I got replaced by a shiny new stamper and thought I had a bad day. Leviathan had a bad day.
Then Asaph turns to the water. God broke open the fountain and the flood.

cards.question: Asaph says God dried up rivers that were ever-flowing.

cards.text: Then Asaph looks up: “The day is Yours, and also the night; You established the moon and the sun.” Day shift, night shift. Both His.

cards.question: Asaph says God set all the boundaries of the earth, and He made the ___ and the ___.

cards.text: Then Asaph goes back to asking. Remember, he tells the LORD, how the enemy has mocked You.

cards.question: Asaph says a ___ people has spurned God's name.

cards.text: Then comes a tender picture. Asaph calls God's people His dove, and friend, my Minty is a dove, so this one gets me right in the apron.

cards.question: Asaph begs God not to hand the soul of His dove over to something. What?

cards.text: Next, Asaph asks God to consider something God made with His people. He's pointing God right back to it.

cards.question: What does Asaph ask God to consider?
Why does Asaph ask God to consider His covenant?

answers.text: Violence fills the dark places of the land
The people have forgotten the covenant
The enemy has written a new law

cards.question: Asaph prays the oppressed won't retreat in shame, and that the poor and needy will ___ God's name.
Near the end, Asaph calls on God to rise up. He says the cause he wants defended belongs to Israel alone, not to God.
In the psalm's last line, Asaph asks God not to disregard something. What?

findings.problem: The opening card has four sentences: 'This is a Maskil…', 'No warm-up.', 'No "How's Your week going?"' and 'His very first line: …'. It also never says what is going on. Nothing hints that the sanctuary lies in ruins, so the baker meets Asaph's 'why' with no context.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: 'Like they own the place' explains what the banners meant. Psalm 74:4 only says they were unfurled 'as signs' and leaves open what they signified. 'Then' also adds an order between the roaring and the banners that the verse doesn't give.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: This card asks the baker to guess the wording of the simile in Psalm 74:5. Card 7 gave nothing about axes or trees, so 'Wielding axes in a thicket of trees' can't be reasoned out over 'Tearing down a tent' or 'Breaking pots'. A baker can only get it right by luck.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: 'Then Asaph asks…', 'He's not asking for a pep talk.' and 'He's asking for that hand.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: 'Then, right in the middle…: Yet.', 'Three letters.' and 'Changes EVERYTHING.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: 'Asaph names one more creature whose heads God crushed' points back to the dragons of the sea on card 3, which is no longer on screen. The question should say what the 'one more' follows.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: 'God fed Leviathan…', 'I got replaced… bad day.' and 'Leviathan had a bad day.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the quoted line from Psalm 74:16, 'Day shift, night shift.' and 'Both His.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This blank tests wording the baker hasn't seen. Card 10 only says the enemy mocked, which doesn't point to 'foolish' over 'mighty' or 'distant'. The baker is left guessing the word Psalm 74:18 uses.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Card 12 only says God's people are called His dove. Nothing in it points to 'Beasts' over 'Hunters', and 'Hunters' is just as natural a threat to a dove. A baker can only get it right by luck.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: Cards 15 through 19 come one after another with no story card, and verses 21 to 23 are never told on any story card. Cards 18 and 19 ask about verses 22 and 23 with no setup told first. Verse 22b ('Remember how the fool mocks You all day long') is never covered at all.

rule.text: Not every choice card needs its own story card right before it: a choice card can follow another choice card when the setup is already told.

findings.problem: No setup comes before this card. In a psalm, 'The prayers of His priests' or 'The songs of His people' are just as natural things to ask God not to disregard. A baker can only reach 'The uproar of His enemies' by luck.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: Card 1 calls Asaph 'one of Israel's psalm writers'. That fact comes from outside the passage (for example Ps 50, Ps 73-83, 2 Chr 29:30), but the card only cites Psalm 74:1. The rules say outside facts need their reference, and that a card's 'verses' field cites exactly what the card uses. The schema has only one 'verses' field.
findings.question: When a story card uses a fact from outside the passage, how should its reference be given? Should it be added to the card's 'verses' field, written in the text, or left out when it only says who a new person is?
